hints: Integrate acceleration with respect to time to find velocity: $v(t) = \int k(3t^2 - 12t + 2)\,dt$.
Use the initial condition $v(0) = 0.4$ to find $C = 0.4$.
Substitute $t = 1$ and $v = 0.1$: $0.1 = k(1 - 6 + 2) + 0.4 \implies 0.1 = -3k + 0.4$, and solve for $k$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the acceleration function $a(t) = k(3t^2 - 12t + 2)$ with respect to $t$ to find the velocity function:
$$v(t) = \int k(3t^2 - 12t + 2)\,dt = k\left(\frac{3t^3}{3} - \frac{12t^2}{2} + 2t\right) + C = k(t^3 - 6t^2 + 2t) + C$$

Use the initial condition $v = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t = 0$ to determine the constant of integration $C$:
$$v(0) = k(0 - 0 + 0) + C = 0.4 \implies C = 0.4$$
$$v(t) = k(t^3 - 6t^2 + 2t) + 0.4$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall that velocity is the indefinite integral of acceleration with respect to time:
$$v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt$$

Integrate the given quadratic expression for acceleration:
$$v(t) = \int k(3t^2 - 12t + 2)\,dt = k\left(t^3 - 6t^2 + 2t\right) + C$$

Apply the initial condition: at $t = 0$, $v = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$0.4 = k(0) + C \implies C = 0.4$$

Write the complete velocity function with $C = 0.4$:
$$v(t) = k(t^3 - 6t^2 + 2t) + 0.4$$

Substitute $t = 1$ and $v = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-1}$ into the velocity equation:
$$0.1 = k(1 - 6 + 2) + 0.4$$
$$0.1 = -3k + 0.4$$

Divide both sides by $-3$ to conclude:
$$k = \frac{-0.3}{-3} = 0.1$$

hints: Integrate $v(t)$ with respect to $t$ to find displacement $s(t)$.
Remember that at $t = 0$, the particle leaves $O$, so $s(0) = 0$, which gives constant $C_2 = 0$.
walkthrough:
Integrate $v(t)$ with respect to $t$ to obtain displacement $s(t)$:
$$s(t) = \int (0.1t^3 - 0.6t^2 + 0.2t + 0.4)\,dt$$
$$s(t) = 0.1\left(\frac{t^4}{4}\right) - 0.6\left(\frac{t^3}{3}\right) + 0.2\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right) + 0.4t + C_2$$
$$s(t) = 0.025t^4 - 0.2t^3 + 0.1t^2 + 0.4t + C_2$$

Since the particle leaves $O$ at $t = 0$, $s(0) = 0$, which gives $C_2 = 0$:
$$s(t) = 0.025t^4 - 0.2t^3 + 0.1t^2 + 0.4t$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the calculus relationship for displacement from velocity:
$$s(t) = \int v(t)\,dt$$

Substitute the velocity formula obtained in part (i) with $k = 0.1$:
$$v(t) = 0.1t^3 - 0.6t^2 + 0.2t + 0.4$$

Combine terms with an arbitrary constant of integration $C_2$:
$$s(t) = 0.025t^4 - 0.2t^3 + 0.1t^2 + 0.4t + C_2$$

Apply the initial displacement condition that motion begins at origin $O$ ($s = 0$ when $t = 0$):
$$0 = 0.025(0)^4 - 0.2(0)^3 + 0.1(0)^2 + 0.4(0) + C_2 \implies C_2 = 0$$

hints: Verify that the sum equals 0, confirming that the particle is at the origin $O$.
walkthrough: Since the displacement $s(2) = 0$, the particle is indeed at the origin when $t = 2\text{ s}$.
teacher_walkthrough:
Substitute $t = 2$ directly into the expression for displacement $s(t)$ derived in part (ii):
$$s(2) = 0.025(2)^4 - 0.2(2)^3 + 0.1(2)^2 + 0.4(2)$$

Add all terms together:
$$s(2) = 0.4 - 1.6 + 0.4 + 0.8 = 0$$
$$\text{Since } s(2) = 0\text{ m, the particle is at the origin } O\text{ at } t = 2\text{ s.}$$
